sourceCopy.name: Image Vectorizer
sourceCopy.title: Image Vectorizer Free | UsefulVerse
sourceCopy.description: Turn simple PNG, JPEG, or WebP artwork into editable SVG paths in your browser. Free local vectorizer.
sourceCopy.intro: Trace simple logos, icons, and flat-color artwork into SVG paths. Choose a color limit and detail size, preview the vector, then download the SVG.
sourceCopy.howQuestion: How do you turn an image into an SVG?
sourceCopy.howAnswer: Choose a raster image, select its output detail and color count, then create the SVG. The tool groups colored pixel runs into real vector paths; edges follow the selected pixel grid, so flat artwork works better than photographs.
sourceCopy.privacyAnswer: No. The image is decoded and traced in this browser tab. It is not uploaded or automatically saved.

fields.imageFile: Choose a PNG, JPEG, WebP, or GIF
fields.mergeRuns: Merge matching path runs to reduce SVG size
fields.detailHint: The longest side is reduced to this many pixels or fewer. Larger detail may create a bigger SVG.
fields.accuracyNote: Best for simple logos, icons, and flat-color drawings. This method follows the pixel grid; it does not smooth curves or reproduce photo detail.
fields.privacyNote: Up to 5 MiB per source image. The image is processed locally and is not uploaded or automatically saved. Large images can use device memory; a computer is recommended.

additionalFaqs.question: Does the SVG contain the original image?
additionalFaqs.answer: No. The result contains SVG path shapes, not an embedded raster image. It approximates the source by grouping pixels into colors and paths.

additionalFaqs.question: Will it vectorize a photograph smoothly?
additionalFaqs.answer: No. The pixel-grid trace is intended for simple logos, icons, and flat-color drawings. Photographs can produce blocky edges and large SVG files.

additionalFaqs.question: Does the tool upload or keep my image?
additionalFaqs.answer: No. The source is processed in this tab and is not uploaded or automatically saved. Processing speed and memory use depend on your device.
